I bet Homemade Ice Cream Sandwiches will be your Summer addiction

Why these homemade ice cream sandwiches are worth the effort

There's a lot to love about making ice cream sandwiches at home. They're a make-ahead dessert, which means you can prep them well before any summer gathering and have them ready to go straight from the freezer. You also get full control over the filling — vanilla, mint chip, cookies and cream, salted caramel, whatever you're in the mood for.

And the edges are where you get to have fun: rolling them in sprinkles, mini chocolate chips, or crushed cookies turns a simple frozen treat into something that looks and tastes a step above anything you'd grab from the grocery store freezer.

How to make ice cream sandwiches

Bake the chocolate base: Line a half sheet pan (roughly 18 by 13 inches) with parchment paper and give it a light coating of cooking spray. Pour your brownie-style batter into the pan and spread it into an even layer. Bake at 350°F for about 15 to 20 minutes, or until a toothpick poked into the center comes out clean. Let the base cool all the way before doing anything else.

Assemble the sandwiches: Once the brownie layer is fully cooled, lift it out of the pan using the parchment edges and slice it lengthwise down the middle so you end up with two equal-sized rectangles. Spread softened ice cream across the top of one rectangle, then gently lay the second rectangle on top, brownie-side up. Return the whole assembly to the freezer for several hours until it firms up, then peel away the parchment and cut into individual squares. Serve straight from the freezer.
